children: AI stocks may be receiving their strongest adoption signal yet: using powerful models is becoming cheaper at a speed the personal-computer industry needed decades to match.

A chart published by venture-capital firm a16z, using Goldman Sachs data, shows an index of large-language-model prices plunging from 100 to roughly 5 in about three years. The measure tracks average pricing per million tokens across models and is indexed to March 2023.

By comparison, the personal-consumption-expenditures price index for computers needed approximately 15 years to reach a similar level during the information-and-communications-technology investment cycle that began in the 1980s.
Why Falling Costs Matter for AI Stocks

The decline becomes more striking after adjusting for model capability. A16z's price-to-intelligence ratio fell close to zero within roughly three years, suggesting customers are receiving more useful computing output for every dollar spent.

For AI investors, that can be a powerful long-term demand signal. Lower prices make models economical for more businesses, applications and everyday tasks. Higher usage could then support demand for data centers, semiconductors, networking equipment, electricity and software built around AI.

But cheaper intelligence is not automatically bullish for every company. Model developers could face shrinking unit prices and intensifying competition, forcing them to generate much larger usage volumes to protect revenue and recover enormous training and infrastructure costs. Companies lacking scale or differentiated products may struggle.

The PC comparison also offers a warning. Falling hardware prices expanded adoption, but value shifted across manufacturers, software businesses and platform owners. AI could follow a similar pattern, creating enormous aggregate demand without allowing every participant to earn attractive returns.

Investors should therefore treat the cost collapse as a strong signal for adoption, not a blanket buy signal. The most durable winners will be companies that convert cheaper AI into greater usage, recurring revenue and sustainable margins faster than pricing erosion undermines their economics.

title: AI Stocks Flash Powerful Signal as Model Costs Collapse
